boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named UNT spaces for making, studying, gathering, viewing art, and joining campus activities.

cards.title: The Spark at Willis Library
cards.subtitle: Willis Library, first floor
cards.notes: Bring a project idea and check the makerspace’s available services before heading over; the first-floor directory places The Spark beside study and technology resources.
cards.short_summary: A named Willis Library makerspace within the library’s first-floor public spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Libraries lists The Spark among Willis Library’s first-floor public spaces and study rooms.
cards.access_notes: Located in Willis Library; confirm current library access and service availability before visiting.

cards.title: Media Commons
cards.subtitle: Willis Library, Room 260
cards.notes: Reserve a station when you need a social, media-focused work session; UNT’s space finder identifies Room 260 as the Media Commons and provides reservations.
cards.short_summary: A reservable social study and media space on Willis Library’s second floor.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Libraries lists Media Commons (Room 260) as a social Willis Library space with station reservations.
cards.access_notes: Station reservations are available; students log in with their EUID to schedule library study spaces.

cards.title: The Nest
cards.subtitle: Willis Library, Room 251S
cards.notes: Use the reservation link to plan a group or media session instead of arriving without a slot; UNT labels this second-floor space social and reservable.
cards.short_summary: A named social space in Willis Library’s second-floor Media Library area.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Libraries lists The Nest (Room 251S) as a social space with station reservations.
cards.access_notes: Station reservations are available; students log in with their EUID to schedule library study spaces.

cards.title: Sarah T. Hughes Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Willis Library, Room 437
cards.notes: Choose this fourth-floor room for a collaborative session near Special Collections; use the library’s space listing to check its current room details and availability.
cards.short_summary: A named fourth-floor collaborative reading room in Willis Library.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Libraries identifies the Sarah T. Hughes Reading Room (Room 437) as a collaborative Willis Library space.
cards.access_notes: Located on Willis Library’s fourth floor; confirm current library access before visiting.

cards.entity_name: Edna Mae Sandborn Music Reading Room
cards.title: Edna Mae Sandborn Music Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Willis Library, Room 430A
cards.notes: Head to the fourth floor when music materials or a collaborative table session fit the task; the floor directory names this room within the Music Library area.
cards.short_summary: A named collaborative reading room in Willis Library’s Music Library area.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Libraries lists the Edna Mae Sandborn Music Reading Room (Room 430A) among Willis Library’s collaborative spaces.
cards.access_notes: Located on Willis Library’s fourth floor; confirm current library access before visiting.

cards.title: Soundbox Music Technology Lab
cards.subtitle: Willis Library, Room 430E
cards.notes: Plan a music-technology work block and verify lab availability first; UNT places Soundbox on the fourth floor alongside music and collaborative study resources.
cards.short_summary: A named music-technology lab within Willis Library’s fourth-floor public spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT Libraries lists the Soundbox Music Technology Lab (Room 430E) among Willis Library’s collaborative spaces.
cards.access_notes: Located on Willis Library’s fourth floor; confirm current library access and lab availability before visiting.

cards.title: Union Art Gallery
cards.subtitle: University Union, second floor
cards.notes: Look behind the main information desk during Union hours to see the current exhibition; the gallery’s program includes student creative work and visual-arts encounters.
cards.short_summary: A second-floor Union gallery dedicated in part to showcasing UNT student work.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT says the Union Art Gallery is behind the main Information Desk on the second floor and showcases UNT student creative output.
cards.source_title: Union Art Gallery — University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: The gallery states that it is open whenever the University Union is open.

cards.title: University Union
cards.subtitle: 1155 Union Circle
cards.notes: Use the building as a meet-up point when your group needs study, lounge, dining, or meeting space; consult the Union map or event schedule for a specific destination.
cards.short_summary: A multi-level student center built for studying, socializing, dining, lounging, and meetings.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT describes the University Union as providing studying, socializing, lounging, dining, and meeting space.
cards.source_title: University Union — University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Building access and individual venue availability vary; check the University Union’s current schedule before planning an event.

cards.title: UNT Community Garden
cards.subtitle: Between President’s EDGE and Legends Hall
cards.notes: Join a workday, volunteer orientation, or gardening workshop to participate; current UNT students, faculty, and staff can apply for a plot regardless of experience.
cards.short_summary: A student-led garden with raised plots, workshops, volunteering, and organic growing.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT says the garden offers volunteer and member opportunities, workshops, and 30 raised plots; supplies are provided and joining has no fee.
cards.source_title: UNT Community Garden — University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Plot membership requires an orientation and availability; workdays and public events are scheduled throughout the year.

cards.title: Pohl Recreation Center
cards.subtitle: 1900 Chestnut Street
cards.notes: Check Recreation Sports programming before going, then use the center as a starting point for organized open-recreation activities and campus wellness events.
cards.short_summary: A named UNT recreation facility used for organized open-recreation programming.
cards.evidence_claim: UNT identifies Pohl Recreation Center at 1900 Chestnut Street and has used it for open-recreation activities including basketball and volleyball equipment checkout.
cards.source_title: Sibling Day — University of North Texas
cards.access_notes: Confirm current Recreational Sports eligibility, hours, and activity availability before visiting.
